stepNotes.1: GraphCommand is the unit's sole export at graph.ts:9, declares graph [sessionID] at line 10, and is registered by cli/boot.ts:23 and :92.
stepNotes.2: The handler only writes stdout, but event-derived tool targets and error labels flow through graph/index.ts:202-215 and :276-285 into unsanitized text renderers; recorded local data is therefore the terminal-output trust boundary.
stepNotes.3: Session lookup is scoped by Instance.provide and shared session-latest helpers; the count===0 return at graph.ts:40-44 is a real format-contract bug because --json emits plain text instead of the empty graph supported by graph/index.ts:117-132.
stepNotes.4: All six non-empty yargs choices reach a matching formatter branch at graph.ts:49-72, --json wins at line 47, and array-returning timeline/topology/ascii outputs are joined consistently.
stepNotes.5: EventQuery.count uses COUNT(*) at query.ts:227-238 before build performs the timestamped row load, adding a second query; the 10,000-row cap bounds memory but can make CLI output partial with only a log warning.
stepNotes.6: The command preserves one-way layering by delegating context, lookup, graph derivation, and rendering; server/routes/graph.ts:74-85 reuses the same GraphFormat surface.
stepNotes.7: All imports and the sole export are live, with no swallowed failures or deferred-work markers; the one-assignment let at graph.ts:32-38 and string cast at :47 are minor readability issues only.
stepNotes.8: execution-graph.test.ts covers four builder scenarios and passed 4/4, but no test invokes GraphCommand; smoke.test.ts:268-286 names graph commands while testing only rollback, compare, and branch.
stepNotes.9: Accepted one Medium zero-event format violation plus Low terminal-safety and long-session completeness advisories; no Critical item exists, so the conditional reverify.md is not produced.
